header.name: repo-proof-index
header.tagline: What each proof claims, and where its evidence lives.

flows.title: How a proof artifact becomes a row a reviewer can scan
flows.footnote: The index does not judge whether a proof is sufficient. It reads what each artifact says about itself, puts that in one row, and leaves the judgment with the reviewer holding the list.
flows.alt: Eight stages of indexing one proof artifact: paths, read, match, row, evidence, relative, table, and exit. Paths are either the files you name on the command line, sorted, or every JSON file in a directory that is scanned when you name none. Each file must hold one JSON object; a list or a string raises before any shape is tried. Six shapes are recognized in a fixed order and the first match wins, with a seventh fallback that catches everything else, so an unrecognized shape still gets a row. Every row carries the same six fields: contract, kind, surface, status, evidence, and path. The evidence line prefers checks that passed, falling back to the first claim, then to a free note, then to a line saying there is no summary. Paths are shown relative to the base you chose, and stay absolute when they sit outside it. The table prints four of the six fields, clipped to fixed widths with a trailing ellipsis, and the contract identifier and the path reach only the JSON output. The exit code is zero once the rows print. Three outcomes: indexed, refused, and not found.

stages.note: Files you name, or a directory scanned.

stages.title: Read
stages.note: One JSON object per file. A list is refused.

stages.title: Match
stages.note: Six shapes tried in order, first one wins.

stages.title: Evidence
stages.note: Passing checks first, then claims, then notes.

stages.title: Table
stages.note: Four columns, clipped, the rest in JSON.

flows.title: How a stack of rows turns into a short list of things to fix
flows.footnote: A short list gets acted on and a long one gets ignored, so the action list stops at eight. The gap count above it is not capped, which is how you tell whether the list you are reading is the whole list.
flows.alt: Eight stages of a review summary: rows, kinds, statuses, gaps, nine, reason, eight, and summary. The rows are every artifact already indexed, in path order. Kinds are counted and sorted by name, so the mix of artifact types is visible at a glance. Statuses are counted the same way. An evidence gap is decided by a string test on the evidence line: empty, the word unknown, or any text beginning with the word no. Nine status values put a row on the action list, among them blocked, draft, drift, fail, planned, unknown, and unverified. The constant status a backend descriptor carries is not among them, so a backend matrix never lands on the list by status alone. Each item names a reason, either to add evidence or to resolve the status it carries, alongside the path that holds it. The list stops at eight items and does not say how many were left out. The summary carries five fields and prints as text or as JSON. Three outcomes: clear, action, and truncated.

stages.title: Rows
stages.note: Every artifact indexed, in path order.

stages.title: Kinds
stages.note: Counted and sorted, so the mix is visible.

stages.title: Statuses
stages.note: Counted the same way, sorted by name.

stages.title: Gaps
stages.note: Evidence missing, unknown, or starting with no.

stages.title: Nine
stages.note: Nine status values put a row on the list.

stages.title: Reason
stages.note: Add evidence, or resolve the status named.

stages.title: Eight
stages.note: The list stops at eight and says nothing more.

stages.title: Summary
stages.note: Five fields, printed as text or as JSON.

returns.label: A GAP IS A STRING TEST, NOT A LOOKUP
A BACKEND MATRIX NEEDS NO ACTION

outcomes.label: CLEAR
outcomes.note: no gaps, and no status on the list

outcomes.label: ACTION
outcomes.note: a status to resolve, or evidence to add

outcomes.label: TRUNCATED
outcomes.note: more than eight rows want attention

cards.title: Every shape a proof file can arrive in, and how it is read

fields.note: The first shape tried. Maturity becomes the status, and the product name becomes the surface the row describes.
The status is a constant, and the evidence counts backends by status rather than naming any one of them.
The verdict becomes the status, and the surface names the witness implementation that produced the receipt.
The evidence line counts claims, checks and action items instead of quoting any of them.
Recognized by an exact module identifier and a summary object, then reduced to counts of entries, organs and receipt kinds.
The bundle status is the worst entry status, in a fixed order: block, then warn, then needs-human, then unverified.
The fallback. Identifier, surface and status are each taken from the first field present out of several candidates.
Order decides. A file carrying a product manifest and a receipt verdict is read as a product use case, and the verdict is never seen.
The stem of the path stands in, so a file with nothing to name it still appears in the index rather than dropping out of it.
The gap test is a string test. A note reading no regressions found is counted as a missing summary, the same as no summary at all.
The file raises before any shape is tried, the command prints one error line, and the exit code is one.

cards.alt: Eleven shapes a proof file can arrive in, one to a row, with what the index reports and why it lands there. A manifest with a product is read as a product use case, taking maturity as the status. A descriptor with backends is read as a backend capability, carrying a constant status and an evidence line that counts backends by status. A receipt with a verdict is read as a witness receipt, taking the verdict as the status and naming the witness implementation as the surface. A packet version and identifier is read as a proof-surface packet, whose evidence counts claims, checks and action items. An exact module identifier with a summary object is read as an organ exchange. A bundle version with entries is read as an organ receipt bundle, whose status is the worst entry status in a fixed order of block, warn, needs-human and unverified. Anything matching none of the six falls back to a plain contract, with identifier, surface and status each taken from the first candidate field present. Recognition stops at the first match, so a file carrying two shapes is read as the earlier one and the later fields are never seen. A file with no identifier borrows the stem of its own path. The accented row is the evidence gap: the test is a string test, so a note reading no regressions found is counted as a missing summary. A root that is not a JSON object is refused before any shape is tried, and the command exits one.
cards.footnote: Recognition runs in a fixed order and stops at the first match, so a file carrying two shapes is indexed as the earlier one. The fallback keeps every file in the index: an unrecognized shape still gets a row, with the file name standing in for an identifier it never carried.
